objects.text: A HyperCity is a real city overlaid with thick information networks that not only catalyze the present but also go back in time to document the past and go forward to project future possibilities.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:001-hyper-multiplicity-and-digital-mapping; parent passage spans printed pp. 6–7.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: “Hyper” adds to, extends, and proliferates: many texts and media, many extensions to and contestations of the historical record, and an infinitely open field of possibilities for participation.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:001-hyper-multiplicity-and-digital-mapping; parent passage spans printed pp. 6–7.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: To address the first question: the book brings together the methods, content, and values of the humanities to create and re-create representations of places, what we are calling“thick mapping.”

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:001-hyper-multiplicity-and-digital-mapping; parent passage spans printed pp. 6–7.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: The final chapter focuses on two world-historical events—the 2011“Arab Spring” in Egypt and Libya, and the Japanese earthquake and tsunami that same year—through the lens of social media mapping.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:002-methods-embodiment-and-the-scale-of-view; parent passage spans printed pp. 8–9.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: After that, the book presents a media archaeology of Google Earth and turns to several cultural-historical investigations of map projections and the political epistemologies of mapping.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:002-methods-embodiment-and-the-scale-of-view; parent passage spans printed pp. 8–9.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: As the book progresses, the long-form narratives break down into smaller and smaller pieces such as data streams, tweets, and images to reveal different perspectives—distant and close—on the mapping of events.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:002-methods-embodiment-and-the-scale-of-view; parent passage spans printed pp. 8–9.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: In the case of Tehran, the maps are attempts to curate the voices and images of protest in the face of powers determined to suppress and erase them.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:003-a-polyvocal-book-built-with-digital-forms; parent passage spans printed pp. 10–11.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: They are each told through the voices of the primary project cartographers and exemplify innovative approaches to creating and deepening public knowledge.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:003-a-polyvocal-book-built-with-digital-forms; parent passage spans printed pp. 10–11.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: The book also features contributions written and designed by project leaders that open up as“windows” onto the HyperCities idea and digital cultural mapping more generally.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:003-a-polyvocal-book-built-with-digital-forms; parent passage spans printed pp. 10–11.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: In this respect, HyperCities are much larger than twenty million inhabitants, since they might embody the entire (largely erased or absent) history of a city—potentially every life, every structure, every street, every voice over time.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:004-hypercities-narratives-through-place-and-time; parent passage spans printed pp. 12–14.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Every story matters, every voice can be heard, every event—no matter how big or how small — can be captured.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:004-hypercities-narratives-through-place-and-time; parent passage spans printed pp. 12–14.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Imagine a search and discovery tool for this web in which you traveled through time and space, rather than inputting keywords in an empty white box.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:004-hypercities-narratives-through-place-and-time; parent passage spans printed pp. 12–14.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Thick maps are not simply“more data” on maps, but interrogations of the very possibility of data, mapping, and cartographic representational practices.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:005-thick-mapping-mapping-as-ongoing-practice; parent passage spans printed pp. 15–19.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Thick maps are sometimes called“deep maps” because they embody temporal and historical dynamics through a multiplicity of layered narratives, sources, and even representational practices.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:005-thick-mapping-mapping-as-ongoing-practice; parent passage spans printed pp. 15–19.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Postmodernism, on the other hand, is supposedly all about surface, the infinite play of signifiers, the total loss of historicity, and the schizophrenic subject called to cognitively map the world in order to somehow brook resistance to the leveling effects of capitalism.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:005-thick-mapping-mapping-as-ongoing-practice; parent passage spans printed pp. 15–19.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: This is why HyperCities is not primarily a“technological” or“computational” problem but foremost a“humanities” problem, namely one of memory, narrative, archival practices, knowledge design, and, finally, ethics.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:006-digital-humanities-and-an-open-future; parent passage spans printed pp. 20–21.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: But over the past decade, the methods, media, and materiality of humanities research have undergone dramatic change, with massive new possibilities emerging for authorship, creative design, meaning-making, data curation, interaction, and dissemination of scholarship.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:006-digital-humanities-and-an-open-future; parent passage spans printed pp. 20–21.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: I wonder: what would it mean to drive downward, into the buried pasts that persist somewhere—in the imagination, in the archive, in the memories of others, in the traces of places long gone and lost?

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:007-the-flaneur-and-the-mediated-city; parent passage spans printed pp. 22–24.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: In other words, maybe the past is always there—quiet, muted, faded, hidden—and it is the task of the flâneur to enable it to speak, to make it come alive and come to light, and, thereby, resonate with the present.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:007-the-flaneur-and-the-mediated-city; parent passage spans printed pp. 22–24.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: But for Walter Benjamin, the German-Jewish cultural critic and philosopher writing his magnum opus, The Arcades Project, a book on nineteenth century Paris, the flâneur was not simply someone who walked the streets of the modern metropolis and disappeared into the swarm of crowds; rather, it was someone who was a time-traveler.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:007-the-flaneur-and-the-mediated-city; parent passage spans printed pp. 22–24.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Subway stops located in the east turned into“ghost stations,” as underground trains originating in the west could no longer stop in East Berlin.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:008-berlin-ruins-and-what-remains; parent passage spans printed pp. 25–26.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: They are man-made mountains of debris, the remains of two million cubic meters of destroyed buildings that were firebombed in the last years of the War.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:008-berlin-ruins-and-what-remains; parent passage spans printed pp. 25–26.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: It’s still there today (you can see it in Google Earth), and it can’t be destroyed because it is too close to residential apartments.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:008-berlin-ruins-and-what-remains; parent passage spans printed pp. 25–26.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: That’s because all of these pasts co-exist, in various degrees, depending on what remains legible and what we care to recognize in the spaces of the present.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:009-berlin-as-a-temporal-and-spatial-palimpsest; parent passage spans printed pp. 27–30.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Not only is space transformed by new media, allowing it to be apprehended and experienced in ways that were previously not possible, but the figure of the flâneur is also transformed, as spectatorship migrates to the screen and eventually the computer interface.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:009-berlin-as-a-temporal-and-spatial-palimpsest; parent passage spans printed pp. 27–30.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: In the mid-1990s, I was hardly the only one to engage in such a critical, cartographic practice of memory and media.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:009-berlin-as-a-temporal-and-spatial-palimpsest; parent passage spans printed pp. 27–30.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Applying the theory of the“simultaneity of the non-simultaneous” as an organizing principle, every lecture began at a place in present-day Berlin (such as Potsdamer Platz or the Olympic Stadium) and then proceeded to“drill down” into the historical layers impacted in these places.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:010-berlin-temporal-topographies-and-hypermedia-berlin; parent passage spans printed pp. 31–34.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Tracing its historical genealogy back to“database” projects such as Ruttmann’s city film and Benjamin’s cultural history of nineteenth century Paris, the goal of Hypermedia Berlin was to construct a web-based platform for representing and studying the cultural, urban, and architectural history of a layered city space.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:010-berlin-temporal-topographies-and-hypermedia-berlin; parent passage spans printed pp. 31–34.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: But rather than taking chronology as the sole organizing principle, I wanted to foreground the uneven time-layers comprising Berlin’s nearly 800-year history, the urban palimpsests, as it were, that form the present.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:010-berlin-temporal-topographies-and-hypermedia-berlin; parent passage spans printed pp. 31–34.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Through the Google Maps and Earth APIs, HyperCities essentially allows users to go back in time to create, narrate, and explore the historical layers of city spaces and tell stories in an interactive, hypermedia environment.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:011-readerly-and-writerly-webs; parent passage spans printed pp. 35–37.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Each time the user moves the map (zooms in, pans, jumps to a new city) or adjusts the time-bar, the application interacts with one or more external servers to retrieve relevant data based on the spatial and temporal bounding coordinates.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:011-readerly-and-writerly-webs; parent passage spans printed pp. 35–37.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Although a web-based platform, HyperCities behaves more like a desktop application because the front-end follows an event-driven programming model rather than a standard webpage submission model.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:011-readerly-and-writerly-webs; parent passage spans printed pp. 35–37.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: The Google Maps/Earth APIs define a set of JavaScript objects and methods, which HyperCities uses to put maps on its interface, allowing instant integration of satellite imagery with other layers such as markers, pathways, images, historical maps, 3D objects, and other kinds of geo-data.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:012-apis-data-and-a-geotemporal-platform; parent passage spans printed pp. 38–41.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Facebook, Google Maps, Yelp, Twitter, and Flickr (to name just a few) expose their data through APIs.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:012-apis-data-and-a-geotemporal-platform; parent passage spans printed pp. 38–41.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: These servers range from commercially available platforms (such as Google’s 3D warehouse,YouTube, and Flickr) to library and archival platforms for maps, GIS data, oral histories, videos, photograph collections, and other media files.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:012-apis-data-and-a-geotemporal-platform; parent passage spans printed pp. 38–41.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: The project began with the protests in Tahrir Square in late January of 2011: what if we could listen to, map, and amplify the voices in the streets of Cairo in real-time and, then, archive those voices for scholars to study in the future?

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:013-from-platforms-to-public-participation; parent passage spans printed pp. 42–48.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Because the front-end relied on components we could not control and which changed all-too-frequently (the Google Maps API and the Google Earth plugin), the project was inherently fragile.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:013-from-platforms-to-public-participation; parent passage spans printed pp. 42–48.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: This shifted the problem of preservation from one of maintaining the visual representations of HyperCities data to opening it to a variety of visual representations using different tools.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:013-from-platforms-to-public-participation; parent passage spans printed pp. 42–48.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Other projects—such as the US Holocaust Memorial Museum’s Darfur genocide map and George Mason’s Archive of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita— utilize the Google Maps/Earth platforms to document and investigate contemporary crises with participatory dimensions for the contribution of data.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:014-thick-mapping-between-gis-and-critique; parent passage spans printed pp. 49–53.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Beyond Google, OpenLayers, an open source mapping platform with a global developer community, and Harvard’s WorldMap, an ambitious, open source platform for exploring, visualizing, and publishing geographic information, are setting new standards for the preservation, dissemination, and analysis of networked geo-data.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:014-thick-mapping-between-gis-and-critique; parent passage spans printed pp. 49–53.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Another project,“Digital Harlem,” also a historical mapping archive, was developed by four historians at the University of Sidney (Stephen Garton, Stephen Robertson, Graham White, and Shane White)“to visualize and explore the spatial dimensions of everyday life in Harlem during its heyday, 1915– 1930.”

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:014-thick-mapping-between-gis-and-critique; parent passage spans printed pp. 49–53.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: At the same time that he made use of zoom, Benjamin was also concerned with things unrepresented on and absent from the Pharus map: social and economic structures, childhood memories, emotions, fleeting images, tastes and smells, noises, textures, and other somatic experiences.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:015-zoom-and-thickness-as-historical-methods; parent passage spans printed pp. 54–57.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: In One-Way Street, for example, the narrative begins quite zoomed in at the street level, at a filling station, before moving into a breakfast room, the Number 113, a visit to Goethe’s house, memories of Chinese curios, the Mexican embassy, and a construction site.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:015-zoom-and-thickness-as-historical-methods; parent passage spans printed pp. 54–57.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Instead, they offer various optics for seeing, remembering, and narrating the urban space, optics that are a function of experience, perception, and zoom level.

provenance.note: Exact quotation candidate inside parent passage passage:015-zoom-and-thickness-as-historical-methods; parent passage spans printed pp. 54–57.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: It would have made little sense to indicate Paris, Basel,Vienna, or even Leipzig and Hamburg on a Berlin map prior to the mid-nineteenth century.

objects.text: In recollecting“images” of his childhood in Berlin, Benjamin pauses on one train station in Berlin in particular: the Anhalter Bahnhof.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: Thick mapping begins to look like an ever-expanding railway system that moves out and downward at the same time, giving rise to a participatory web of intersecting cities, voices, streets, memories, and narratives.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation

objects.text: It makes little sense to speak of “before” or“after” or necessity as a modality of movement; instead, we get temporally layered, spaces of possibility, marked by distance and proximity, contingency, simultaneity, and networks of connection.

objects.transcriptionStatus: normalized text extraction; page image / PDF review required before publication as a typeset quotation
